title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: PagerDuty connectors for escalation policies and on-call schedules
summary: The briefing passes: the deployment controls, licensing, defaults and roadmap facts are supported. It correctly reports the conflicting Microsoft guidance on changing access permissions; minor corrections concern a source attribution and checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans a Copilot connector for PagerDuty escalation policies and on-call schedules.
claims.quote: Customers can connect M365 Copilot with PagerDuty to access escalation policies and on-call schedules with Copilot Connector.

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Open questions
claims.claim: The target is December CY2025, a month already past on the run date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2025"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.claim: The record supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap does not name the two individual connectors.
claims.quote: Customers can connect M365 Copilot with PagerDuty to access escalation policies and on-call schedules with Copilot Connector.

claims.claim: Learn documents a connector that indexes PagerDuty escalation policy data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The PagerDuty Escalation Policies Microsoft 365 Copilot connector enables your organization to index PagerDuty escalation policy data to make it available to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Search.

claims.claim: Learn documents a separate connector integrating PagerDuty schedules into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: The PagerDuty Schedules Microsoft 365 Copilot connector integrates PagerDuty schedule data into Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Escalation policy content can surface in Copilot, Copilot Search and Microsoft Search.
claims.quote: When you deploy the connector, Copilot, Copilot Search, and Microsoft Search can surface relevant escalation policy information directly within apps like Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and SharePoint.

claims.claim: Schedule information can surface in Copilot, Copilot Search and Microsoft Search.
claims.quote: By using this connector, Copilot, Copilot Search, and Microsoft Search can surface schedule information directly within apps like Teams, Outlook, and SharePoint.

claims.claim: The Schedules connector is currently in preview and might have limited availability.
claims.quote: Preview status – This connector is currently in preview and might have limited availability. Preview features are subject to change.

claims.claim: The Schedules preview is subject to change.
claims.quote: Preview features are subject to change.

claims.claim: The escalation policies connector indexes policy metadata.
claims.quote: Escalation policy metadata: Policy ID, name, summary, description, and URLs.

claims.claim: Indexed escalation rules include minutes before an unacknowledged incident escalates.
claims.quote: including the number of minutes before an unacknowledged incident escalates away from this rule

claims.claim: Indexed escalation rules include incident assignment targets.
claims.quote: and the targets an incident should be assigned to upon reaching the rule.

claims.claim: The connector indexes services associated with each escalation policy.
claims.quote: Service associations: Services that use each escalation policy.

claims.claim: The connector indexes teams linked to escalation policies.
claims.quote: Team relationships: Teams linked to escalation policies (for Advanced Permissions).

claims.claim: The escalation policies connector supports only full crawl.
claims.quote: The PagerDuty Escalation Policies connector only supports full crawl.

claims.claim: The escalation policies full crawl runs daily by default.
claims.quote: The default schedule of the full crawl is set for every day.

claims.claim: Escalation rule details are indexed by default.
claims.quote: The following properties are indexed by default. ... ruleDetail

claims.claim: Linked services are indexed by default.
claims.quote: The following properties are indexed by default. ... usedByServices | Not applicable | The services associated with the escalation policy.

claims.claim: Audit properties labelled createdBy, createdDateTime, lastModifiedBy and lastModifiedDateTime are indexed by default.
claims.quote: The following properties are indexed by default. ... createdBy ... createdTime | createdDateTime ... lastModifiedBy ... lastModifiedTime | lastModifiedDateTime

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The connectors require admin deployment before indexing, so the default state is admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: To deploy the connector, choose Create in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The PagerDuty Schedules Copilot connector starts indexing schedules from your PagerDuty account right away.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The escalation policies connector starts indexing immediately after Create.
claims.quote: Select Create to deploy the connection. The PagerDuty Escalation Policies connector starts indexing content right away.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Manage access permissions says updating access permissions after connection creation is unsupported.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Escalation policies are visible to all users in the organisation by default.
claims.quote: Everyone in the organization: All indexed escalation policies are visible to everyone in your Microsoft 365 organization. This is the default setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: When PagerDuty Advanced Permissions is enabled, escalation policy access in Search and Copilot is limited to linked-team members.
claims.quote: When Advanced Permissions is enabled in PagerDuty, only members of the teams linked to a specific escalation policy can access and search for that escalation policy in Microsoft Search and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The same linked-team limitation applies to schedules when Advanced Permissions is enabled.
claims.quote: When Advanced Permissions is enabled in PagerDuty, only members of the teams linked to a specific schedule can access and search for that schedule in Microsoft Search and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Indexing escalation policy audit properties requires a PagerDuty Business or Enterprise plan licence.
claims.quote: A PagerDuty Business or Enterprise plan license is required to index the following data properties: createdBy, createdDateTime, lastModifiedBy, and lastModifiedDateTime.

claims.claim: The connector authenticates through a PagerDuty OAuth 2.0 app.
claims.quote: In PagerDuty, add a new app with OAuth 2.0 functionality enabled.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An admin enters the OAuth app Client ID and Client Secret into connector authentication.
claims.quote: To use PagerDuty OAuth for authentication, enter the Client ID and Client Secret you obtained from your PagerDuty app registration settings in the prerequisites section.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The escalation policy app setup calls for Read Access scopes for Audit records, Escalation Policies, Teams and Users.
claims.quote: Audit records – Read Access; Escalation Policies – Read Access; Teams – Read Access; Users – Read Access

claims.claim: Developers can use the connector as a knowledge source for declarative agents built with Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Developers can use this connector as a knowledge source in declarative agents they build with the Copilot Studio, Agent Builder, or the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

claims.claim: Developers can use the connector as a declarative agent knowledge source in Agent Builder.
claims.quote: Developers can use this connector as a knowledge source in declarative agents they build with the Copilot Studio, Agent Builder, or the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

claims.claim: Developers can use the connector as a declarative agent knowledge source with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.
claims.quote: Developers can use this connector as a knowledge source in declarative agents they build with the Copilot Studio, Agent Builder, or the Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[0].note; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The documented route to change access permissions is deletion and recreation with Custom setup.
claims.quote: In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection. Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.claim: The escalation policies overview conflicts with the permissions page by saying access permissions can be customised later.
claims.quote: Admins can configure the access permissions during connector deployment or customize them later through the connector settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: When connection failures prevent reliable delete detection, items not rediscovered for 28 days are removed from the index.
claims.quote: If connection failures prevent delete detection from running reliably, items that aren't rediscovered during crawls for 28 days are automatically removed from the Microsoft 365 index to maintain compliance.

claims.claim: Indexing synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licences.
claims.quote: Indexing of synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licenses.

claims.where: front matter: licensing model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Synced connector grounding and agents are included with Microsoft 365 plus the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 + Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on | ✅ | ✅ | ✅

claims.where: front matter: licensing notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E7 also supports synced connector Copilot grounding and agents.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E7 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅

claims.claim: The licensing table lists Microsoft Search only for a Microsoft 365 plan alone.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 (any plan) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio licensing row supports synced connector agents without Copilot grounding.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 + Copilot Studio license | ✅ | Agents only (no Copilot grounding) | ❌

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go row supports synced connector agents without Copilot grounding.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go | ✅ | Agents only (no Copilot grounding) | ❌

claims.claim: Connector grounding in Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 Copilot licences and has no extra charges.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.

claims.where: front matter: licensing notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The PagerDuty connector pages publish no connector-specific price or meter at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: PagerDuty connector pricing meter cost license. Opened both PagerDuty overviews and deployment guides and connector prerequisites; these publish plan prerequisites and general indexing entitlement, not a PagerDuty-specific price or meter.

claims.where: Scope; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: AI administrator is required to deploy and manage connectors and access staged rollout.
claims.quote: To configure and deploy Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: A PagerDuty admin must complete OAuth setup, attributed to the connector prerequisites page.
claims.quote: Set up OAuth prerequisites | PagerDuty admin
claims.fix: Replace the attribution with: 'The PagerDuty Schedules deployment guide assigns OAuth prerequisite setup to a PagerDuty admin.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/pagerduty-schedules-deployment.

claims.claim: The escalation policies deployment guide says the deployer must be a Microsoft 365 admin.
claims.quote: You must be a Microsoft 365 admin.

claims.claim: A PagerDuty account with administrator permission is a prerequisite.
claims.quote: You have a PagerDuty account with administrator permission in the PagerDuty app.

claims.claim: The PagerDuty environment must allow API access.
claims.quote: The PagerDuty environment is configured to allow API access.

claims.claim: The OAuth app registration uses Scoped OAuth.
claims.quote: Select Scoped OAuth in the PagerDuty new app registration setting page.

claims.claim: The instance REST API URL depends on whether PagerDuty uses the US or EU service region.
claims.quote: For the US service region: https://api.pagerduty.com; For the EU service region: https://api.eu.pagerduty.com

claims.claim: Schedules default to only people with access to the content in the data source.
claims.quote: Users | Access permissions | Only people with access to the content in the data source

claims.claim: Staged rollout supports up to 100 users.
claims.quote: You can add up to 100 users and 15 Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Staged rollout supports up to 15 Microsoft 365 groups.
claims.quote: You can add up to 100 users and 15 Microsoft 365 groups.

claims.claim: Staged rollout settings apply to all Search and Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Staged rollout settings are applicable to all Search and Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: Staged rollout limits result visibility subject to existing access permissions rather than replacing them.
claims.quote: When the rollout finishes, only the users and groups you specified see connector data in results, depending on their permissions.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Access permissions are configured through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > PagerDuty Escalation Policies > Custom setup > Customize user settings > Access permissions.
claims.quote: select Copilot > Connectors. ... Select the Gallery tab. ... select PagerDuty Escalation Policies. ... select Custom setup. ... Customize user settings ... Access permissions

claims.claim: No API is documented for this prebuilt connector's connection-level access-permissions choice.
claims.quote: Searched: graph externalConnection access permissions everyone PagerDuty connector configure API. Read deployment and manage-access-permissions; Graph connection management and beta resource/update references show no operation for this choice. Item ACL APIs do not document this setting.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Staged rollout is edited at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connection > Staged Rollout > Edit.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. ... Find the connector that you want to modify. ... In the Staged Rollout column, next to Staged, choose Edit.

claims.claim: No API is documented for connector staged rollout audience settings.
claims.quote: Searched: connector staged rollout audience API Microsoft Graph. Read staged-rollout and Graph connection management and beta resource/update references. Results document the admin UI, not a connector rollout API; Entra featureRolloutPolicy concerns a different feature.

claims.claim: Copilot Visibility is found at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connection > Copilot Visibility.
claims.quote: Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connection that you want to modify. Under Copilot Visibility, select the toggle to turn the connector on or off

claims.claim: No API is documented for the Copilot Visibility toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Visibility connector toggle API Graph. Read manage-connector and Graph connection management and beta resource/update references. No operation is documented as setting this toggle; enabledContentExperiences lists search, not a Copilot Visibility property.

claims.claim: Turning off Copilot Visibility does not stop crawling the data source.
claims.quote: If the connection is off, it can still crawl the data source, but the data isn't used for search results.

claims.claim: Turning visibility off excludes the connection from Copilot Search and Copilot Chat results and responses.
claims.quote: When the visibility is off, the connector is excluded from all Copilot Search and Copilot Chat results and responses.

claims.claim: Visibility changes can take up to 30 minutes to propagate.
claims.quote: After you update the visibility settings at the connection level, allow up to 30 minutes for the changes to propagate across all Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: Learn describes Copilot Visibility for partner connectors and does not explicitly establish its reach over these Microsoft-built PagerDuty connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Visibility connector toggle API Graph; PagerDuty Copilot connectors deployment access permissions. Read manage-connector and both PagerDuty deployment guides/overviews. Visibility is described for partner connectors, without naming these prebuilt connectors.

claims.claim: Delete is found at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > connection > Delete.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections. Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. ... In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection.

claims.claim: DELETE /v1.0/external/connections/{connectionsId} deletes an external connection and removes its indexed items.
claims.quote: Deletes an externalConnection object. ... DELETE /external/connections/{connectionsId} ... DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr

claims.claim: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy restricts the app to connections it is authorised to manage.
claims.quote: The app can only read and write external connections that it is authorized to, or it can create new external connections.

claims.claim: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All allows the app to read and write all external connections.
claims.quote: Allows the app to read and write all external connections without a signed-in user.

claims.claim: Graph's connection-management guide describes managing connections the app created or was explicitly authorised to manage.
claims.quote: You can only view and manage the connections that you created or were explicitly authorized to manage.

claims.claim: The cited Graph management documentation does not specifically explain deleting gallery-created connections.
claims.quote: Searched: Graph delete external connection created Microsoft 365 admin center gallery. Read Graph connection management, delete reference and permission descriptions. They document general connections and authorisation, not gallery-created connections explicitly.

claims.claim: Connection states are shown on Your Connections after deployment.
claims.quote: You can view the connection state for your deployed connectors on the Your Connections tab in the admin center. The state shows in the Connection state column.

claims.claim: Permanent crawl failures mark a connection Failed and produce service health notifications.
claims.quote: If a permanent failure occurs, the connection is marked as Failed, and notifications are sent to the service health dashboard under the Issues section for your organization to act on.

claims.claim: The connection details pane shows configured access permissions.
claims.quote: Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane. Under Permissions, you can view the permissions set for the connector.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout
claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks the reader to check or configure is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Decide who may read escalation policies and schedules'; 'Confirm ... Advanced Permissions'; 'register the OAuth app'; 'Check the connection state'. Table covers escalation-policy access, staged rollout, Copilot Visibility and delete.
claims.fix: The checklist's schedules access setting, PagerDuty Advanced Permissions and OAuth app settings, and connection-state monitoring have no corresponding controls row. Remove these checklist instructions if strict checklist/table alignment is required; do not add rows as part of this correction.
